Run a command in a pod, capture stdout/stderr/exit code

Source: R/stream.R
pod_exec.Rd

Higher-level one-shot wrapper over pod_exec_open() for the common case: "run this and tell me what happened". Blocks until the remote command exits and the connection closes.

Usage

pod_exec(
  client,
  namespace,
  name,
  command,
  container = NULL,
  stdin_data = NULL,
  timeout = 60
)

Arguments

client

An ApiClient (typically kube()$client).

namespace

Namespace of the pod.

name

Pod name.

command

Character vector: the command and its arguments.

container

Optional container name (required if the pod has more than one container).

stdin_data

Optional character or raw vector to send on stdin before closing the input channel.

timeout

Wall-clock cap in seconds (default 60). Sessions that exceed it are forcibly closed; timed_out = TRUE is set on the result.

Value

A list with stdout (character), stderr (character), exit_code (integer or NA), and timed_out (logical).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
k <- kube()
r <- pod_exec(k$client, "default", "nginx-abc", c("ls", "-la", "/"))
cat(r$stdout); message("exit ", r$exit_code)
} # }
